summary: George A. Kennedy was a sinologist and linguist who studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1932–1937) under Erich Haenisch and Otto Franke. He held a post at Yale University from circa 1936 to 1960.

Keyworth is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He studied at UC Santa Barbara and earned his PhD at UCLA under Robert E. Buswell Jr., later serving at the University of Colorado Boulder and the University of Saskatchewan.

George Abraham Grierson was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Trinity College Dublin. He served in the Indian Civil Service, directed the Linguistic Survey of India (1898–1928), and was a Governor of SOAS University of London (1917–1925).

George Adolphus Jacob was an Indologist. He held posts as a colonel in the Bombay Staff Corps (attested 1888) and the Indian Army (attested 1909), and was a Fellow at the University of Mumbai (attested 1894).

George Baumann is an Indologist who earned his PhD at Heidelberg University and studied librarianship in North Rhine-Westphalia. He held positions at the University of Tübingen and served as a Bibliotheksreferendar at its library from 1976 to 2001.
George C. O. Haas was an Indologist who served as Recording Secretary for the American Oriental Society (~1912–1918) and as editor of the Journal of the American Oriental Society (~1916–1920).

George Cardona was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at NYU, Yale (doctoral supervisor Paul Thieme), and with traditional teachers in India. From circa 1965, he served as Professor of Linguistics at the University of Pennsylvania.

George Chemparathy is an Indologist and philosopher who studied under Erich Frauwallner and Paul Hacker. He held posts at Loyola College, Chennai, and as a professor at Utrecht University (attested 1983–1987).

George Cowgill was an archaeologist and historian who studied at Stanford University and Harvard University. He held academic posts at Brandeis University (~1960–1990) and Arizona State University (from ~1990).
George Croom Robertson was a philosopher who studied at the University of Aberdeen and University College London. He held a post at University College London from circa 1866 to 1892.

George Cœdès was a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and archaeology. He studied at EPHE and Berlin, directed the National Library of Thailand (1918–1929), and served as director of the École française d'Extrême-Orient (1929–1947).

George D. Bond is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at the University of Sri Lanka and earned his PhD at Northwestern University, where he served as Professor of Religion from circa 1974.

George David Birkhoff studied at the University of Chicago and Harvard University. He held academic posts at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, Princeton University, and Harvard University (1912–1944).

George Eugene Dunkel is an Indologist and linguist who earned his doctorate at the University of Pennsylvania. He taught at Johns Hopkins and Princeton before holding the chair for Indo-European studies at the University of Zurich in 1986.

George Foot Moore was a scholar of religion educated at Yale and Union Theological Seminary. He was a professor at Andover Theological Seminary (1883–1902) and Frothingham Professor of the History of Religion at Harvard University (1904–1928).
George Herbert Palmer was a philosopher who was educated at Phillips Academy and Harvard University. He spent his academic career holding a post at Harvard University from circa 1870 to 1913.

George L. Hart is an Indologist and linguist who completed his PhD in Sanskrit at Harvard University (~1964–1971). He taught Sanskrit at the University of Wisconsin-Madison before becoming a professor at the University of California, Berkeley circa 1975.

George Lakoff is a linguist and philosopher who studied at MIT and Indiana University Bloomington. He taught linguistics at Harvard University (1965–1969) and served as Professor of Linguistics at the University of California, Berkeley (1972–2016).

George Melville Bolling was an Indologist and linguist educated at Loyola University Maryland and Johns Hopkins. He held professorships at the Catholic University of America (1895–1913) and Ohio State University (1914–1939), and served as president of the LSA.

George Quasha is a scholar in religious studies, Tibetology, and other fields who founded Station Hill Press. He held teaching posts at Stony Brook University, Bard College (~1974–1999), The New School, and Naropa University.
